biography.plain_text: Harry Bauer was an American lawyer and electricity executive who served as president and chairman of Southern California Edison. A University of Southern California law graduate, he helped establish Bauer, Wright and MacDonald in 1921. His civic responsibilities included leading the Automobile Club of Southern California and serving as a Caltech trustee.

long_biography.plain_text:
In 1930, Harry Bauer paid for three Caltech undergraduates to investigate how other universities housed their students. They visited colleges in the eastern United States and travelled to Oxford, Cambridge, Heidelberg and the Sorbonne. The purpose was to help Caltech's students assess dormitories and fraternity houses for their own campus. He also contributed towards completing Fleming House.

His support for learning included the history of science. In 1955 he financed the purchase of early scientific books from Count Giampaolo Rocco of Bologna, arranged by Caltech dean Earnest C. Watson. The acquisition became a central part of the institute's rare-book collection.
